A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same thought-MDP research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM arithmetic evaluations in Table 1 and gridworld learning experiments in Figure 2, with additional model validation in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds gridworld experiments with shifted sub-goals in Appendix E and Figure 3.

M1.justification: The thought-action mechanism, causal-transformer policy, behavior-cloning pre-training, and REINFORCE learning procedure are retained. The finite-horizon appendices extend the mathematical analysis rather than introduce a changed learning algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds a gridworld scenario in which each evaluation sub-goal is shifted by one cell while pre-training retains the original tasks. This introduces a limited mismatch between learned skills and evaluation requirements; the original gridworld and arithmetic tasks remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same eleven LLMs and Thinking/No Thinking conditions. The gridworld comparisons retain Pretrained-Think, Pretrained-NoThink, Scratch-Think, and Scratch-NoThink, including in the new experiment.

E3.justification: The existing experimental protocols are retained. Appendix E explicitly reuses the pre-training procedure, and Figure 3 retains success-rate/thinking-time measurements and 200 episodes per iteration. The added task scenario and its repeated-run information are changes under E1 and E5.

E4.justification: Appendix E and Figure 3 add a targeted robustness test asking whether thinking remains useful when pre-trained sub-policies no longer exactly solve the evaluation task. The original thinking/pre-training ablations and prompted-model validation are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 2 newly displays individual training runs while retaining five trials and 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. Figure 3 reports ten trials for the new scenario using the same interval convention; this is not an increase in the original experiment's trial count.

E6.justification: New Figure 3 shows Pretrained-Think reaching near-unit success under shifted sub-goals while the other agents remain near zero; Appendix E reports that Pretrained-NoThink no longer learns to solve this task. These are new results under changed conditions. Table 1's numerical results are unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendices B and C extend the discounted formulation to time-homogeneous, undiscounted finite-horizon thought MDPs, with time-dependent policies and values. They add Assumptions 9–10, Proposition 11 and its proof with environment-action tie-breaking, and Theorem 12 and its policy-improvement proof. This substantially expands the formal scope.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: thought MDPs, initialization-dependent emergence of thinking, thinking as local policy improvement, supporting LLM evidence, and a non-language proof of concept. The new material supports these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds a hypothesis that finite-sample on-policy learning explains why thought actions persist despite the non-thinking optimality result. Appendix B also explains the time-homogeneity restriction: in time-varying environments, waiting could itself improve future opportunities.

D1.justification: Section 6 adds an explicit code-access link and clarifies that pre-training task resampling occurs at each time-step. The hardware, optimizer settings, learning rates, and action-masking details from v1 Appendix C are retained in v2 Appendix E. The PDFs document the access claim but do not establish external availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of rational metareasoning, Dynamic Thinker, and visual or latent reasoning, with corresponding citations. It revises the Thinker comparison from fixed thinking duration versus learning when to think to model-based planning versus model-free thought control. The broader positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose remain intact, with localized wording, notation, and paragraph-heading edits. v2 adds acknowledgments and a conference checklist, inserts the finite-horizon appendices, and renumbers the retained prompt and implementation appendices.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with individual-run traces and revised labeling, and a new two-panel Figure 3 presents the robustness experiment. Figure 1 and both tables are retained, with appendix relocation and page reflow rather than a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's discounted treatment and exactly aligned gridworld skills, v2 adds an explicit finite-horizon analysis and evidence that thinking remains useful with imperfectly matched skills. Individual-run plots, a code-access link, and discussion of persistent thinking improve transparency and interpretation. These are useful gains, while the main empirical evidence and conclusions remain largely unchanged and limited to simple tasks.
